questions.prompt: How many backend surfaces does the Agronomy Studio frontend call directly?
questions.explanation: The frontend talks to exactly two surfaces — the gateway at /agronomy-api/* and the mock AI search — regardless of how many domain services sit behind the gateway.
options: Two: the gateway and the mock AI search
Zero; it reads from a static cache

questions.prompt: Environment parity means the frontend uses different request paths and payload shapes in local development than it does in production.
questions.explanation: Parity means the opposite: the paths and response shapes are identical across environments. Only the mechanism answering the request (local mock server vs. Netlify functions) changes.

questions.prompt: What is the main risk of having the frontend call all twelve domain services directly?
questions.explanation: Direct calls leak base URLs, versions, and auth into the frontend, so backend changes force frontend redeploys. A single gateway lets the UI depend on a stable contract instead.
options: Infrastructure details like URLs and auth leak into the UI, coupling it to backend changes
It makes the AI search deterministic
It removes the need for any gateway tests
